Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Sri Lanka's second innings! Dimuth Karunaratne and Nishan Madushka are in the middle to open for the hosts while Shaheen Afridi will take the new ball for Pakistan. Here we go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Sri Lanka, on the other hand, started off well with Prabath Jayasuriya getting three quick wickets but they faded away after that. They reduced the visitors to 101/5 but let them get away with it as their bowlers lacked the sharpness. That big partnership between Salman and Shakeel has cost them a lot as they now trail by149  runs. Mendis finished with a five-wicket haul while Vishwa Fernando and Kasun Rajitha chipped in with one each. Now, it is up to their batters to get them back in this Test. Join us in a bit for their second innings.

Pakistan have finally been bowled out for 461! A brilliant maiden double hundred from Saud Shakeel stole the show. They showed great determination in their batting performance especially. The top order didn't contribute much except for Shan Masood but the massive 177-run 6th wicket stand between Agha Salman and Shakeel took the visitors out of a difficult situation and not only that it helped them to surpass Sri Lanka's total and take a healthy lead of 149 runs, but the former just missed out on his century. Shakeel remained unbeaten and managed well with the tail-enders to keep the runs flowing while Nauman Ali, Naseem Shah, and Abrar Ahmed also chipped in with the required support and some crucial runs in the end.

OUT! CAUGHT! All over for Pakistan! Fraction short and spins into the middle and leg. Abrar Ahmed pulls this to the long leg region where Angelo Mathews runs around at the boundary and takes a fine catch. Pakistan are dismissed for 461 taking a lead of 149 runs. Saud Shakeel remains unbeaten on 208 and he has played a knock for the ages here.

SESSION SUMMARY -  76 runs and 2 wickets in 25 overs. Another session that belonged to Pakistan! Saud Shakeel has been impressive once again as he went past  150 with ease but he did give one opportunity to the hosts which was spilled by Angelo Mathews. Sri Lanka managed to get the breakthrough when Ramesh Mendis got rid of Nauman Ali who held one end well and soon after Vishwa Fernando dismissed Shaheen Afridi as well. However, they struggled to build on that even after taking the second new ball and let visitors gain control of his match as they lead by 77 runs now. Naseem Shah and Shakeel have been very patient and are tiring out the bowlers with scoring runs as well. Also, not having a review has also cost the hosts a bit. They will hope to quickly get the remaining wickets after Tea while Pakistan will look to extend the lead even further. Join us at 3.45 pm IST (10.15 am GMT) to see how things pan out.

Saud Shakeel and Agha Salman started off where they left last evening and milked runs with ease. They carried on with their attacking mindset and added a mammoth 167 for the 6th wicket. Salman played a poor shot and perished for a well-made 83. Saud Shakeel batted through the session and got to his 2nd Test hundred. Nauman Ali has looked solid and is playing the support role well to Shakeel. Pakistan will hope to carry on and extend their lead in the next session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 3! The two umpires are making their way out to the middle while the Sri Lankan players are in a huddle just outside the boundary ropes. They spread out to take their respective field positions. Saud Shakeel and Agha Salman stride out to crease for Pakistan. Kasun Rajitha to start proceedings with the ball. Also, due to the delay Lunch will be taken at 12.45 pm IST (7.15 am GMT) and Tea at 3.25 pm IST (9.55 am GMT). 91 overs to be bowled and each session will be two hours long barring further rain.
Good news folks! We have a start time and that is 10.45 am IST (4.15 am GMT) which is just moments away from now.

Update - 10.25 am IST (4.55 am GMT) - The groundsman are still working hard to remove the water from the outfield so that play can start. However, there is still no word from the ground in regards to the start time. Stay with us for further updates.

Update - 9.43 am IST (4.13 am GMT) - There was huge overnight rain and some a bit earlier too so the outfield is pretty wet at the moment. The start of Day 3 will be delayed but it shouldn't be a long one as the groundstaff are working hard to make the ground ready.

Pakistan batted with positive intent and were almost scoring at five runs per over for the most part of their batting innings. However, they lost half their side by just over 100 runs and looked into trouble. The duo of Saud Shakeel (69*) and Agha Salman (61*) got together and stitched an unbeaten 120 runs for the 6th wicket under 25 overs. The batting approach from visitors has been refreshing, they are just 91 runs behind Sri Lanka’s total. Pakistan will hope to take a healthy lead while the hosts will want to break this stand quickly and get into the visitors' lower order. Let’s see how the day pans out for both sides. Stay tuned as we shall bring you the live-action in a short while.

Sri Lanka got past 300 in their first innings on the back of a magnificent hundred by Dhananjaya de Silva while Angelo Mathews made a solid 64. The lower order added some valuable runs and took Sri Lanka to a reasonable total. Shaheen Afridi, Naseem Shah, and Abrar Ahmed took three wickets each while Agha Salman took the solitary wicket of Sadeera Samarawickrama finishing an above-par effort with the ball.

Hello, and a warm welcome to our coverage of Day 3 in this first Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka played at the Galle International Stadium in Galle. The game is nicely poised with Pakistan trailing by just 91 runs in reply to Sri Lanka’s first-innings total of 312. Day 3 is supposed to be the moving day in the Test and we can expect plenty of action.
…DAY 3, SESSION 1…

It was obvious that Sri Lanka will throw Prabath Jayasuriya from one end but his magic didn't sustain long after the second session as Pakistan were scoring easily. Sri Lanka shuffled their bowling pack but didn't work out. Earlier on Day 2, Dhananjaya de Silva got his century as he along with the tail helped Sri Lanka get over 300. However, we feel Pakistan have a slightly upper hand now. Join us on Day 3 at 9.35 am IST (4.05 am GMT). Till then, cheers!

It is STUMPS. The conditions do not get better and the umpire calls the end of Day 2. So, Pakistan will be the happier side. The stand between Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel somewhat replicates that of Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva. Pakistan after losing the top order with nothing much needed to get back on track. Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel looked in full control as they got to their fifties and were looking to add more before the rain showed up.

Pakistan though will be relieved to see a stand building and will hope Agha Salman and Saud Shakeel go onto make a big score in the final session. They kept on losing wickets regualrly. Sarfaraz Ahmed tried to be proactive but even he didn't last long. A big stand is needed by these two Pakistani batters.
